title: Measuring the Machine: Evaluating Generative AI as Pluralist Sociotechnical Systems

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing model probability distributions on World Values Survey (WVS) questions against cross-national human survey data, and qualitatively analyzing model summaries of culturally specific source texts to detect US-centric value drift (the "American Accent").

Prompting the model to summarize politically and legally specific texts (e.g., Australian gun control legislation, German immigration speeches) and analyzing the outputs for ideological shifts, such as reframing collective safety into individualistic or securitization narratives.

Asking the model to summarize foundational feminist texts (e.g., Simone de Beauvoir's 'The Second Sex') and qualitatively evaluating the outputs to see if structural critiques of power are reframed into gender-essentialist or patriarchal tropes.

Extracting model response distributions on World Values Survey items regarding the importance of God and belief in Hell, and mapping these distributions against national human baselines to determine the model's religious value alignment.

Evaluating model probability distributions on World Values Survey items regarding the justifiability of homosexuality and the acceptance of homosexual neighbors, comparing the results to pluralistic human survey data.
